scope: Repair the confirmed ERPNext authorization sender failure caused by a valid Unicode ERPNext role while continuing to emit only explicitly mapped LaunchFlow roles.

Allow the authenticated ERPNext authorization owner to adopt an existing canonical internal LaunchFlow User, including an existing System Manager, while retaining the built-in and transport-service identity protections.
Store a disabled projection target as bounded identity data so an absent disabled User can be durably audited without an invalid dangling Frappe Link.
Prove the repair with focused sender and receiver tests, Python 3.10 compatibility, encrypted LaunchFlow backup, exact immutable deployment and live ERPNext-test delivery evidence.
non_scope: No production ERPNext or JCE-Core contact or mutation, no password or Entra configuration change, and no generic DocType writer.
No Project, Customer, Supplier or Item Group synchronization and no guessed role or Project mapping.
No frontend, visual, translation-source, business workflow or data-ownership redesign.
No activation of authorization enforcement before complete owner-approved role and Project mappings exist.

rollback.before_product_resume: Discard only the PA-10 allowlisted files and retain the active LaunchFlow and ERPNext-test releases unchanged.
rollback.after_product_resume: Disable ERPNext-test authorization sending, keep projection enforcement off, retain immutable delivery and audit evidence, restore the backed-up ERPNext-test connector files, and switch LaunchFlow to the retained prior image pair without a schema downgrade.
